name: TimeoutBudget
purpose: Attach a monotonic deadline to an inbound request and propagate the remaining budget to every downstream call so no call outlives its originating request.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol
from contextvars import ContextVar

class TimeoutBudget(Protocol):
    deadline_ns: int
    origin: str
    def remaining_ms(self) -> int: ...
    def for_call(self, max_ms: int) -> int: ...
    def expired(self) -> bool: ...

CURRENT_BUDGET: ContextVar[TimeoutBudget | None] = ContextVar('current_budget', default=None)
invariants: Every outbound call MUST use min(local_timeout, TimeoutBudget.remaining_ms()) and NEVER the local timeout alone.
The deadline MUST be measured on a monotonic clock and SHALL NOT move backward on wall-clock jumps.
A call issued when remaining_ms is not positive SHALL be refused before any socket I/O begins.
The budget CANNOT be extended inside the request scope; extensions FORBIDDEN without a new request boundary.
The budget SHALL be propagated across task boundaries via the context variable, never via thread-local state.
extension_contract: Adopters bind a DeadlineSource adapter to ingress (HTTP header, gRPC deadline, CLI flag) and register a propagation middleware for each transport client so the remaining budget is written into outbound headers (e.g. grpc-timeout, X-Deadline-Ms).
consumption_example:
async def fetch_profile(uid: str) -> Profile:
    budget = TimeoutBudget
    call_ms = budget.for_call(max_ms=250)
    return await http.get(f'/profile/{uid}', timeout_ms=call_ms)

why_essential: Per-call timeouts set locally diverge from the caller's real deadline, allowing a chain of retries to exceed the inbound SLA by multiples and convert a slow dependency into a stampede of zombie work.
alternatives_considered: Static per-client timeout: cannot shrink as the request ages through hops.
Server-side cancellation only: wastes client and network resources before the server decides.
Budget enforced via exception unwinding: triggers too late to free downstream resources.
